clue.text: Afterthought about covering trials by judge in Scotland

definitions.note: plural noun phrase matching a plural answer

indicators.note: about means the afterthought's letters sit around the covering word

parts.note: PS, a postscript, is an afterthought added to a letter
a roof is a covering over a building

explanation.surface: A late thought concerning the cover-up of Scottish judge-only trials.
explanation.walkthrough: In Scots law a proof is a civil trial heard by a judge sitting without a jury.
explanation.definitionFit: Scottish legal term for a hearing before a judge alone, with no jury present.

clue.text: Fundamental law of capital for an auditor

indicators.note: an auditor is a listener, so the word for capital is to be heard rather than seen

parts.note: capital, the sum of money lent or invested, is the principal

explanation.surface: A basic rule about how capital is treated, as an accountant would see it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auditor' suggests accounts, but here it is simply a hearer; principal and the answer sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A basic truth or rule underpinning a system of thought or conduct.

clue.text: Old beer for a time of revolution

definitions.meaning: a strong ale traditionally brewed in the tenth month, a historic name for it
the Russian Revolution of 1917 is named after the month it happened in

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a strong ale once brewed in autumn, and the month of the Bolshevik rising.

clue.text: Confound the management, treading one under foot!

parts.note: to floor someone is to confound or baffle them
the board is a company's management

explanation.surface: Baffle your bosses while trampling one of them!
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: the item you tread on underfoot is a plank of the floor.
explanation.definitionFit: A plank forming part of the walking surface of a room, stepped on constantly.

clue.text: Postscript we see a theologian finish with hesitation

parts.note: DD, Doctor of Divinity, is the standard crossword theologian
an end is a finish
um is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: We read a cleric's ending, delivered with much humming and hawing, as an afterthought.
explanation.definitionFit: Something added at the end of a book or letter as a supplement.

clue.text: Sacking one's son in miserable circumstances

indicators.note: in means the first pieces are placed inside the word for miserable

parts.note: dismal means miserable or gloomy; the phrase reads as in dismal circumstances
one is I, and with 's it gives IS

explanation.surface: A man's son is fired in wretched conditions.
explanation.definitionFit: Firing an employee from a job, which is what sacking means.

clue.text: A king thus upset Aphrodite's son

parts.note: ER, Edwardus Rex, is the royal cipher of a King Edward

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the word for thus is turned upside down

parts.note: so means thus, in this way

explanation.surface: A monarch accordingly upsets the son of the goddess of love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns SO into OS, after ER.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek god of love, child of the goddess of love in Greek myth.

clue.text: Vessel in port, on the forward-looking serviceman's right?

indicators.note: in means the vessel word sits inside the port's name

parts.note: Deal is a port on the Kent coast
a can is a vessel or container

explanation.surface: A ship docked in harbour, on the starboard side of a sailor facing ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Serviceman' suggests the forces but means a worshipper at a church service: facing the altar, the dean's (south) side of the choir is on the right. DEAL is a Kent seaport.
explanation.definitionFit: Belonging to the dean's side of the choir, south of the aisle, to a worshipper's right facing east.

clue.text: Mozart's source a song in this language?

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it starts, its first letter

parts.note: a lay is a song or ballad

explanation.surface: Was a song in this tongue where Mozart drew his inspiration?
explanation.definitionFit: The tongue spoken in Malaysia and parts of Indonesia.

clue.text: The way the old eye trouble occurs

parts.note: St, street, is a way
ye is an old spelling of the

explanation.surface: How optical problems used to arise.
explanation.definitionFit: An inflamed swelling on the eyelid, a minor eye complaint.

clue.text: Hymn, a popular one, breaks into a canter

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: breaks into means the letter for one is pushed inside the gait

parts.note: a trot is a gait close to a canter
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A well-liked hymn bursts into a lively canter.
explanation.definitionFit: A psalm or chant sung as the priest approaches the altar at the start of Mass.

clue.text: Unflappable, though a colt is loose

indicators.note: loose means the letters of a colt is are set free to rearrange

explanation.surface: Calm even though a young horse has got out.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing stoic patience: calm and uncomplaining in hardship.

clue.text: Swiss capital invested in extremely chancy movement to do with communication systems

indicators.note: invested in means the capital's name is clothed by the other letters
extremely means take only the outermost letters of chancy

parts.note: a tic is an involuntary movement
Berne is the capital of Switzerland, in its French-style spelling

explanation.surface: Swiss money put into a very risky venture concerning communications.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invested in' and 'capital' suggest finance. BERNE sits between CY (the first and last letters of chancy, from 'extremely') and TIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the science of control and feedback in machines and living systems.

clue.text: Sole contribution to navigation Lysander made

indicators.note: a contribution to the phrase is a part of it, so the letters are found inside those words

explanation.surface: The single thing Lysander added to navigation.
explanation.definitionFit: Being the single one, with no other, as in a sole heir.

clue.text: Liqueur made a rich man so tipsy

indicators.note: tipsy means unsteady, so the letters of a rich man so reel into a new order

explanation.surface: A drink that got a wealthy man drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet cherry spirit distilled from the marasca cherry.

clue.text: Returned traveller joins cast to act in play

indicators.note: returned means the traveller word comes back, read from right to left

parts.note: a rep, sales representative, is a commercial traveller
a form is a cast or mould

explanation.surface: A salesman back from his trip joins the cast of a stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: To play a part on stage, to present a role.

clue.text: Plant found by girl on both sides of ravine

indicators.note: the girl's name is split to stand either side of the ravine word

parts.note: Mary is a girl's name
a chine is a deep ravine, as on the Dorset and Isle of Wight coasts

explanation.surface: A flower discovered by a young woman either side of a gorge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks botanical but means industrial equipment. A chine is a coastal ravine in southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Industrial plant is the heavy machines and equipment of a factory.

clue.text: Bird said originally to roll about in mud

indicators.note: originally means take the first letter of said

parts.note: to wallow is to roll about in mud, as pigs do

explanation.surface: A bird reportedly began by rolling in the mire.
explanation.definitionFit: A swift-flying migratory bird with a forked tail.

clue.text: These town characters use it as a sharpener

indicators.note: characters are letters, so the letters of these town are taken as material to rearrange

explanation.surface: Townsfolk sharpen things with it.
explanation.definitionFit: A stone used to hone the edge of blades and tools.

clue.text: Terrible crime, smothering sanctimonious old quack

indicators.note: smothering means the jumbled letters cover the word for sanctimonious
terrible means the letters of crime are mangled

parts.note: pi, short for pious, means sanctimonious

explanation.surface: A dreadful offence suppressing a self-righteous charlatan of former days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terrible' turns crime into EMRIC, and 'smothering' puts PI inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic term for a practitioner relying on experience alone, hence a charlatan doctor.

clue.text: A country girl's reading

parts.note: Peru is a South American country
Sal is a girl's name, a short form of Sally; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: What a rural young woman reads.
explanation.definitionFit: A careful look through a text, an act of examining it.

clue.text: Escaped charge for disclosure of secrets

definitions.meaning: electric current lost through faulty insulation, charge that gets away
the unauthorised passing of confidential information to outsiders

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses involve something slipping out: electricity from a circuit, or confidential facts to the press.

clue.text: State of a couple of graduates seen around Los Angeles

indicators.note: seen around means the graduates appear close by the city, next to it in the run

parts.note: BA and MA, Bachelor and Master of Arts, are two graduates
BA and MA, Bachelor and Master of Arts, are two graduates

explanation.surface: The condition of two college leavers spotted in Los Angeles.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the fifty US states, in the Deep South.

clue.text: Burns church?

parts.note: not something on fire but the word Robert Burns, the Scots poet, would use for a church

explanation.definitionFit: The Scots word for a church, as used by Scotland's national poet.

clue.text: This food upset Ruth King

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the pieces are turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: Babe Ruth was the famous American baseball player
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: This dish disagreed with a woman called Ruth and a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like indigestion but reverses BABE plus K.
explanation.definitionFit: Pieces of meat grilled on a skewer, a takeaway dish.

clue.text: The lowest form of travel? Quite the opposite

definitions.text: The lowest form of travel? Quite the opposite

parts.words: The lowest form of travel? Quite the opposite
parts.note: at school the lowest form or class is the first, but on trains and planes the class so named is the highest

clue.text: Singular method of government

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
a way is a method

explanation.surface: A unique way of running a country.
explanation.definitionFit: Rule or dominion, as in holding a nation under one's control.

clue.text: But are these clothes really worthless?

definitions.text: But are these clothes really worthless?

parts.words: But are these clothes really worthless?
parts.note: a slang word for clothes is also a word for failures or useless things, so the question asks whether the garments live up to the name

explanation.definitionFit: Slang for garments, and also for things that turn out useless.

clue.text: In a Swiss canton, copper is used for this bridge

indicators.note: in means the copper symbol is placed within the canton's name

parts.note: Basle (Basel) is a Swiss canton
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

clue.text: This movement is energetic, thanks to a soldier starting it

indicators.note: starting it means the soldier pieces come at the front of the rest

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
ta is British informal for thanks

explanation.surface: A musical passage gets lively thanks to an army man setting it going.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is everyday British slang for thank you.

clue.text: Accurate shot from a small window

definitions.meaning: a hit on the very centre of a dartboard or target
a round thick pane or circular opening, as in old ships and buildings

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a dead-centre hit on a target, and a little round window.

clue.text: Comfort for an aircraftman in 13

indicators.note: in means the aircraftman's abbreviation goes inside the word from 13

parts.note: 13-across is defined as sole, which is the word used here
AC is the RAF abbreviation for aircraftman

explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference is to the word clued at 13-across, which was defined as Sole.
